blocks.content: Rocks inside the Earth are constantly subjected to forces generated by plate movements. These forces create stress, which leads to deformation known as strain.
When the elastic limit is exceeded, rocks fracture suddenly — producing an earthquake.

rows: Bends and returns to original shape

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Forces from plate movements subject subterranean rocks to continuous stress.
Stress induces rock deformation, which is formally known as strain.
Below the elastic limit, rock deformation is elastic and reversible.
Exceeding the elastic limit leads to sudden rock fracture, triggering earthquakes.
Strain is defined as the physical deformation of rock caused by applied stress.
Earthquakes occur specifically when stress exceeds a rock's elastic limit, resulting in sudden rupture.

cells: Forces rocks to slide past each other

blocks.content: When stress remains below the elastic limit, rocks bend but return to their original shape. When the elastic limit is exceeded, rocks fracture suddenly — producing an earthquake.
